name: Tunday Kababi
why_it_matters: Founded 1905 by Haji Murad Ali — the one-armed (tunday) chef who reportedly won a Nawab's contest for kebabs soft enough to eat without teeth. The galouti recipe blends 100+ spices and has stayed in the family across four generations.
insider_tip: The original Akbari Gate shop is the cramped, no-AC heart of the operation; service is fast but seating is bench-style. Cash strongly preferred. Buffalo meat is the default — chicken galouti is on the wider menu but skip mutton on busy nights when turnover is faster on the buffalo lines.
signature_address: Shop 3, Masjid Usmania Choori Wali Gali, Akbari Gate, Chowk, Lucknow 226003

name: Tunday Kababi
why_it_matters: The Aminabad branch of the 1905 Tunday line — newer fit-out, AC seating, the same family recipe. Where most travellers actually end up eating because the original Chowk shop is logistically harder.
insider_tip: Sits beside Wahid Biryani; do both in one visit if you're kebab-and-biryani serious. Expect 15-20 min wait at peak; the ground-floor takeaway counter is faster.
signature_address: 168/6, Old Nazirabad Road, Mohan Market, Khayali Ganj, Aminabad, Lucknow 226018

name: Idrees Biryani
why_it_matters: Founded 1968 by Mohammad Idrees — the reference point for Lucknawi-style yakhni biryani in the Chowk old city. Slow-dum cooking with separate meat and rice stages, rather than the layered Hyderabadi technique.
insider_tip: Open only in afternoons (~12:30pm) and sells out by 4-5pm — call ahead or come early. Limited indoor seating; takeaway is the local norm.
signature_address: 41, 29241, Victoria Street, Idris Hotel, Raja Bazar, opposite Patanala Police Station, Lucknow 226003

name: Wahid Biryani
why_it_matters: Established 1955 in a narrow Nazirabad lane — that original tiny shop still operates beside the larger Aminabad outlet. Rated by Lucknow regulars as the chicken biryani benchmark; Mohd. Azharuddin and several PMs are on the visitors' wall.
insider_tip: Sits next to Tunday Kababi — order a half-plate of galouti from there to eat alongside the biryani; locals do this combination routinely.

name: Raheem's Kulcha Nahari
why_it_matters: Established 1890 in a narrow Akbari Gate lane opposite Tunday Kababi — slow-cooks nihari for ~2.5 hours over coal and wood, paired with tandoor-baked kulcha layered with milk and ghee. The morning ritual locals describe with the most reverence.
insider_tip: Strictly a breakfast operation — arrive before 11am or the nihari is gone. The kulchas come hot from the tandoor; ask for one at a time so they don't cool on the plate.
signature_address: Akbari Gate, opposite Tunday Kababi, Chowk, Lucknow 226003
